root_idea.summary: The root has two principal semantic directions: support accompanied by esteem, and striking or restraining.
root_idea.development: The support branch extends to strengthening, aiding, and honoring; the striking branch yields disciplinary punishment, understood as restraint from harmful conduct.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested Form II verb has distinct lexical uses of support and honor and should appear as its own public form.

senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrences, the object is a person or group receiving support; the support may be understood as warding off harm or opposition.
A Quranic use expressing reverence toward the person honored, alongside or in a context of giving due respect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prevent, hinder, withhold, forbid, or turn someone away from a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I; also constructed with عَنْ الشيءِ, “from the thing.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To tie a cord around a camel’s upper nostrils in order to put medicine into its mouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized veterinary construction of Form I.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To approach sexually or have sexual intercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct Form I usage; the construction does not imply a general restriction on the sex or status of the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To discipline, chastise, correct, or punish someone so as to turn them away from evil or foul conduct.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II; the action is characterized as corrective restraint.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To beat or flog; in legal usage, to inflict a discretionary punishment below a fixed legal penalty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related verbal nouns عَزْرٌ and تَعْزِيرٌ are used; descriptions of intensity range from moderate beating to vehement beating, while the legal sense is specifically non-fixed punishment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To compel someone to do something and instruct them by preventing a return to contrary conduct; especially, to teach religious obligations and ordinances.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II disciplinary and instructional construction, also associated with تَعْزِيرٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To blame, censure, or reprove someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct Form II usage, with a corresponding Form I variant also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To abase someone or render them abject, vile, despicable, or ignominious.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported contrary sense to honoring or venerating.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of the Angel of Death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper name, retained as a separate lexical item rather than treated as a verbal sense of عَزَّرَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of a prophet, Uzayr.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper name mentioned in Quran-focused lexical discussion; it is not a Form II verb sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A surname for a long-necked water bird, identified with the سَبَيْطَر or, in another account, the crane.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate bird name and kunya-like expression.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Form I prevention and turning-away meaning.
Form II corrective discipline and punishment.
Beating, flogging, and discretionary legal punishment.
Compulsion and instruction in religious obligations.
Aiding, strengthening, and warding off opposition.
Proper name of the Angel of Death.

cautions: The public Quranic headword is normalized to the Form II perfect citation form عَزَّرَ rather than the inflected QAC lemma display candidate.

The Form I prevention branch and the Form II disciplinary, supporting, and honoring branches are kept distinct; the proper names and plant and bird names are separate lexical items, not additional Quranic verb senses.
